title: AI Security Engineer (f/m/d)
locationText: Berlin or Hamburg, Remote within Germany, Cape Town, UK, or Serbia
description:
Clariness is looking for an AI Security Engineer (f/m/d) based Germany, UK, SA, or Serbia.
- Full-time; unlimited -

About the role:

This role is about building, operating and continuously improving Clariness’ security capabilities across applications, cloud infrastructure and AI systems. As our founding-level security hire, you will establish the security engineering function, define its priorities and work directly with engineering teams to embed effective security controls throughout our technology environment.

As an AI Security Engineer, you would be responsible for:

• Defining Clariness’ security engineering strategy and roadmap, and building and operating the security function across application security, cloud security, AI and LLM security, vulnerability management and supporting security tooling.

• Working directly with engineering teams on secure system design, threat modelling, penetration testing and vulnerability remediation, while embedding appropriate security controls into development processes and CI/CD pipelines.

• Owning AI security and governance across LLM-powered features, RAG systems and agentic pipelines, including assessing and mitigating risks covered by the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

• Designing and validating safeguards for AI agents, including sandboxing, privilege and access controls, secure tool use and adversarial red teaming of AI systems.

• Evaluating, deploying and continuously improving AI-powered security automation, including autonomous vulnerability triage, LLM-powered alert analysis, compliance evidence gathering and AI-assisted threat intelligence.

• Assessing commercial and open-source security tools based on effectiveness, operational fit and cost, and developing custom solutions where existing tooling does not meet Clariness’ requirements.

• Managing Clariness’ IT security compliance programme-including SOC 2 Type II, applicable EU AI Act high-risk obligations, GDPR Article 32 technical measures and GxP IT security controls-while maintaining audit-ready documentation and acting as the primary security liaison for external auditors, regulators, Legal and Compliance.

We would like you to have: 

• At least five years of hands-on experience in security engineering, application security or information security, with strong technical depth beyond advisory or governance responsibilities.

• Proven experience building or significantly developing a security programme within a product engineering environment, ideally as an early or founding security hire.

• Strong practical experience across application security, cloud security, secure software development, threat modelling, penetration testing, vulnerability management and security controls within CI/CD pipelines.

• Experience assessing, testing or implementing security controls for LLM-powered applications, RAG systems or agentic pipelines.

• Hands-on experience with AI agents, either building them for security automation or securing them through adversarial testing, sandboxing and privilege controls.

• Demonstrable compliance experience involving at least one SOC 2 audit cycle, GDPR programme ownership or implementation of EU AI Act requirements, including the ability to produce audit-ready documentation and work with external auditors.

• Experience in a regulated industry such as clinical research, pharmaceuticals, healthtech or fintech, with knowledge of GxP or comparable regulated data-handling requirements considered a strong advantage, alongside strong English communication skills at C1 level.

You may ask now, why should I work for you? Let us give you a few reasons - and you'll learn more during the process.

• A varied and exciting job with a lot of personal responsibility in an international company, where you can develop and expand your skills.

• Professional and personal development opportunities - incl. personal development budget.

• Flexible working hours and mobile working.

• Regular team events

title: Founding Partner (Fractional Head of People)
description:
About Respiris

Respiris is built to ensure that no one faces career transitions alone.
We are creating a modern alternative to traditional outplacement by combining human connection, structured coaching, community, and AI-enabled tools to support individuals during some of the most important and vulnerable moments of their professional lives.
We partner with companies to support employees with greater care, consistency, and credibility during workforce change. Respiris sits at the intersection of service, community, and technology, creating a model that is both deeply human and built to scale.
This is not legacy outplacement with a new label. This is a new category built for how work, networks, and transitions actually happen today.
About the Opportunity
Respiris is building a network of Founding Partners to activate and grow markets across the United States.
This opportunity is designed for experienced operators who have already generated meaningful independent revenue and want to add outplacement as a high-margin, relationship-driven revenue stream.
As a Founding Partner, you are not reselling a centralized service. You are building the market with us.
You will deepen relationships with existing clients, create new entry points into organizations navigating workforce change, and position yourself at the center of one of the most critical moments in the employee lifecycle.
This is an additional revenue stream designed to complement and expand your existing income portfolio.
What You’ll Do

• Build and activate a local market within your existing network

• Develop relationships with CHROs, Heads of People, CFOs, Legal leaders, Founders, and executives

• Position Respiris as a trusted partner for outplacement and transition support

• Generate introductions, referrals, and partner company relationships that convert into revenue

• Deliver structured coaching to individuals navigating career transitions

• Facilitate engagements across a three-month lifecycle (10 sessions per engagement)

• Host or support curated events (e.g., Stranger to Friends) to build trust and visibility

• Collaborate directly with the Founder on market activation and growth

• Use AI-enabled tools to improve execution, organization, and coaching quality

• Build a repeatable revenue stream layered into your existing work

Requirements
What Makes a Great Founding Partner

• You have experience as a Head of HR, HRBP, recruiter, advisor, or operator

• You have generated at least $50,000 in revenue under your own EIN (required)

• You understand how to build and manage client relationships

• You are trusted by senior decision-makers

• You are comfortable navigating sensitive employee transition moments

• You can turn relationships into revenue opportunities

• You are highly relational and commercially minded

• You are comfortable using modern tools and AI platforms

• You are willing to invest time, effort, and capital into building a market

Non-Negotiable Requirement
All candidates must have generated a minimum of $50,000 in independent revenue under their own EIN, regardless of current employment status (W-2, founder, advisor, or otherwise).
This ensures Founding Partners have demonstrated the ability to build, sell, and deliver independently.
What This Is Not
This is not a fit if you:

• Have not generated independent revenue

• Do not have an EIN or business activity

• Are looking for passive leads

• Want a traditional salaried role

• Are uncomfortable with relationship-driven selling

• Are not prepared to invest financially

•
Respiris accelerates operators. It does not create them.

How the Model Works
Respiris is a B2B company. We sell to organizations, not individuals.
Founding Partners generate revenue through:

• Existing client relationships

• New executive relationships

• Workforce transition events

Each engagement averages $1,500 and includes:

• Ten sessions over three months

• Structured coaching

• Flexible scheduling

• AI

title: Technical Program Manager, Robotics
description:
About the Team
Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of physical systems.

About the Role

As a Technical Program Manager, Robotics Facilities, you will serve as the Robotics point-of-contact for cross-functional partners supporting the design and construction of Robotics sites. You will consolidate requirements, priorities, and decisions across Robotics disciplines and route those inputs through your counterpart, who manages design and construction partners and coordinates their workstreams.

You will clarify requirements, coordinate technical and operational inputs, manage dependencies and changes, and drive timely decisions through planning, design, construction, commissioning, and handover. This role calls for sound program judgment as research and operational needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role, you will:

- Consolidate requirements, priorities, and decisions across Robotics research, engineering, and operations teams, providing the Real-Estate Workplace counterpart with a clear and coordinated view of Robotics needs.

- Translate Robotics workflows and equipment needs into documented requirements for floor layouts, utilities, network connectivity, environmental conditions, material flow, physical access, and operational support, working with technical owners to define acceptance criteria.

- Coordinate Robotics design reviews, ensuring technical owners assess proposals, resolve open questions, and confirm that agreed requirements are reflected in project documents.

- Track Robotics deliverables and dependencies against project milestones, surface risks and changes early, and secure decisions needed to keep work moving.

- Coordinate with Legal, Finance, Security, IT, Environmental Health & Safety, and other specialists to resolve issues affecting Robotics requirements and readiness.

- Coordinate Robotics readiness for equipment installation, moves, commissioning, and operational handover, with clear ownership and follow-through.

- Identify facility constraints that slow experimentation or operations, and use feedback from Robotics teams to improve requirements and handover practices for future projects.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have experience leading technical programs involving hardware and physical infrastructure, ideally in robotics, laboratories, advanced manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

- Can reconcile competing priorities across technical and operational teams and translate evolving needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria.

- Can read drawings and technical documentation, ask useful questions about building systems and equipment interfaces, and involve specialists at the right time.

- Bring disciplined program management across requirements, schedules, dependencies, risks, decisions, and change management.

- Are comfortable moving between technical detail and broader program priorities across multiple concurrent efforts, focusing teams on decisions and dependencies that affect progress.

title: Provider Operations Coordinator
description:
Our Story

TopDog Law is not your typical law firm. We're a nationally scaling personal injury firm built for impact and growth - owning the client experience end-to-end, from marketing and intake through litigation. We believe that world-class marketing, paired with exceptional legal talent and operations, creates better experiences and outcomes for clients and the business alike.

Over the past three years, we've grown 2-3x year over year, setting a new standard on the marketing side of the personal injury space and proving what's possible when strategy, speed, and execution align. Now we're applying that same discipline and innovation to firm operations, case management, and national scale - intentionally building the infrastructure, systems, and teams to grow without sacrificing quality, culture, or accountability.

We are a fully remote team that share trust, open communication, and a commitment to doing great work. If you love ownership, thrive in a fast-moving environment, and want to help build something exceptional, you'll feel right at home here.

The Opportunity

The Provider Operations Coordinator helps the provider lane run, and is essential for timely and active follow up. The Provider Relations team, including the field provider-relations role and the leaders who hold provider meetings and outreach, own the relationship and are the first point of contact with each provider. This role owns what happens behind that relationship: making sure that once a provider is connected, everything the firm needs from them is requested, received, documented, and entered accurately.

Working like an executive assistant to the provider team, the coordinator sends the firm’s provider materials after a meeting, creates and tracks follow-ups, and works directly with each provider’s admin and front-office staff to collect the remaining information needed on the firm’s side. The coordinator is then responsible for getting that information into the firm’s systems cleanly, so provider records are complete, consistent, and usable by case teams. This person is also the backup for when our relations team is connecting actively with providers to answer the phone and make sure there is quick connection for escalating needs or providers hoping for connection, and help with coordinating in-field adjustments if our in-field representative is in a meeting already.

This role is administrative and detail-driven by design. It frees the provider team to spend its time in the field building relationships, while ensuring no provider falls through the cracks between the first conversation and a complete, usable provider file.

What You Will Own

Provider Follow-Up and Admin Outreach

• Support the Provider Relations team after each provider meeting or outreach contact by sending the firm’s one-pager and related provider materials and drafting and sending the follow-up.

• Create and maintain a follow-up cadence for every newly connected provider, so open items, next steps, and owners are always visible to the team.

• Serve as the day-to-day administrative contact with provider admin and front-office teams, requesting and chasing the remaining information the firm needs on its side.

• Escalate relationship, pricing, or policy questions back to the Provider Relations team rather than handling them directly; keep the provider’s relationship owner informed of anything outstanding.

Provider Data Collection and Documentation

• Track what has been received and what is still missing for each provider. For example, contact and office information, billing and records-request details, locations, and specialties, and follow up until the file is complete.

• Enter and update provider information in the firm’s systems (e.g., Filevine and the provider tracking tool) accurately and on a consistent timeline.

• Support clean provider mapping so each provider and location is recorded once, consistently, and linked correctly to the cases and records that reference

title: Systems Engineer
description:
Systems Engineer
Middleware Platform, Azure, Microsoft Windows Server, Monitoring, Automation and AI
Location: Remote - Pune or Baroda
Experience: 4-6 years
Shift: 24×7 rotation, including planned maintenance windows and change events
Role summary

• You will keep our Middleware Platform, Azure and Windows server estate running day to day - responding to alerts, resolving incidents within SLA, Product/Application deployment, executing changes cleanly, and steadily improving the stability of the systems in your care.

• You work within established processes and alongside Team Engineers and Database Administrators, taking ownership of your own queue and escalating appropriately.

• This role also carries a real automation mandate. We expect you to notice repetitive manual work and remove it - through scripting, through Azure automation tooling, and increasingly through AI agents that handle routine operational tasks.

Experience

• 4-6 years in systems administration, Application and infrastructure support or cloud operations.

• Minimum 4 years hands-on production Azure administration (not lab, training or certification-only exposure).

• Minimum 3 years administering Windows Server in production.

• Experience working to SLAs in a ticket-driven support environment.

• Willing and available to work rotating 24×7 shifts and out-of-hours maintenance windows.

Preferred qualifications

• Graduation or Above

• Healthcare or other regulated-industry experience.

Key responsibilities

• Azure platform administration

• Administer Azure infrastructure day to day; provision, resize and decommission Azure resources following documented standards and approved change requests.

• Support Azure PaaS workloads including App Services - deployments, configuration, scaling and restarts.

• Apply resource tagging, cost-optimisation recommendations and policy compliance actions as directed.

• Alert monitoring and response

• Own the alert queue on your shift. Monitor Logic Monitor, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and the enterprise monitoring platform; acknowledge, triage and action alerts within SLA.

• Investigate alerts using KQL queries in Log Analytics, Application Insights telemetry and Windows Event Logs.

• Identify duplicate or non-actionable alerts and propose tuning - threshold changes, aggregation windows, suppression rules. Flagging a bad alert is part of the job, not an optional extra.

• Maintain monitoring coverage and visibility: report agents that are down or resources missing from monitoring, and build/maintain dashboards and workbooks that surface system health to the team.

• System stabilisation

• Resolve incidents end to end; support the Team Members during major incidents with diagnostics, evidence gathering and communication updates.

• Contribute to root cause analysis - collect logs and timelines, document findings, and implement the corrective actions assigned to you.

• Perform proactive health checks across applications, servers and Azure resources: disk, CPU, memory, service state, certificate expiry, backup success.

• Build knowledge of application architecture, help create and update application and alert-handling documentation, and perform pre/post product functionality checks.

• Track recurring issues in your queue and raise them as problem records rather than repeatedly applying the same workaround.

• Perform performance troubleshooting using standard OS and Azure diagnostic tools.

• AI agent development and process automation

• Write and maintain PowerShell scripts for routine administration: user and resource provisioning, health checks, reporting, scheduled tasks and cleanup jobs.

• Optional: Build automation using Azure Automation Runbooks, Logic Apps and Power Automate, with proper authentication via managed identity and alerting on failure.

description:

Founded in 2001, ttcInnovations is a certified woman-owned consulting and talent partner supporting Fortune 500 organizations. We connect clients with top-tier experts through staff augmentation, project delivery, and flexible engagement models, always prioritizing culture fit and impact.
Today, we’re evolving alongside traditional learning services into a business transformation and performance partner. Our work is increasingly focused on diagnostic-led engagements that drive measurable outcomes across performance consulting, change management, enablement, and sustainment.

Location: Remote (U.S.)

Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Change Management Consultant to support clients through complex transformation initiatives. This role embeds structured change management strategies into learning and enablement solutions, ensuring initiatives drive adoption, reduce resistance, and accelerate measurable business outcomes.
The consultant operates in a client‑facing, advisory capacity and partners closely with business leaders, HR, L&D, and internal design teams to integrate change strategy with learning and execution.

• Partner with client stakeholders to assess change readiness, organizational impact, and adoption risk.

•

• Stakeholder identification and engagement

• Resistance identification and management

• Support the development of change enablement assets, including:

•

Preferred Qualifications

• Consulting, advisory, or professional services experience.

What Success Looks Like

• Recommended solutions are embedded within a clear, structured change approach.

title: Test Engineer
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Test Engineer Teams

We’re seeking an exceptional Test Engineer to join our Germany-based team focused on localising and advancing Wayve’s autonomous driving technology for the German market. This is a unique opportunity to play a hands-on role in shaping our AV capabilities in Germany from the ground up.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Test Engineer, you'll independently own the design and delivery of automated verification for a defined area of our embedded software stack. You'll build robust, reusable test automation, drive failures to root cause across engineering boundaries, and steadily raise the bar on coverage, reliability, and traceability. This is a hands-on delivery role with room to grow into broader areas of the system including sensing and model-behaviour testing as the company and your experience evolve. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with a sharp eye for improvement across multiple engineering domains.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

- Develop automation for system functionality tests at component, integration, and system levels, across software and hardware boundaries.

- Automate open-loop and closed-loop replay based Tests, reliability and fault-injection tests to support verification, release, coverage expansion, and debug workflows.

- Lead root-cause investigations for failures found during test campaigns, collaborating across hardware, software, and infrastructure teams.

- Optimise buildkite CI/CD-integrated test workflows for rapid, reliable, and repeatable execution.

- Integrate third-party verification tools including JAMA (requirements), MC/DC (coverage), and MISRA (style compliance); manage artefacts via Artifactory and Azure.

- Define and track KPIs and quality metrics for system testing, supporting data-driven validation and release decisions.

- Uncover software and hardware bugs through increased test coverage and report findings through JIRA.

- Identify and implement infrastructure improvements that enhance test coverage, failure traceability, and compliance reporting.

- Review, create, and adhere to Risk Assessments to ensure all testing activities are conducted safely and responsibly.

 

🙌 You should apply if

ESSENTIAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

- Hands-on experience with system-level verification and validation in robotics, embedded software, or mechatronic systems, with a track record of delivering test automation independently.

- Experience with L2+ hands-off, L3, or L4 automated driving systems.

- Knowledge of consumer safety-rating protocols (e.g., Euro NCAP -AEB, LSS/LKA, ADAS scenarios), DCAS regulatory testing (UN R171), and automotive cybersecurity testing and standards (ISO/SAE 21434, UN R155).

- Experience with HiL testing and tooling using CAN, Ethernet, GMSL, dSPACE, Vector, Xylon, or similar.

- Strong proficiency in Python, including developing automation test frameworks with pytest.

- Proven ability in interface-level testing, including hardware/software interactions and embedded interfaces.

- Experience integrating software quality assurance tools and standards (ASPICE, SOTIF, ISO 26262, JAMA, X-RAY).

- Knowledge of open- and closed-loop HiL replay using dSPACE or other emulators.

- Proficient in CI/CD principles and related tooling (e.g., GitLab CI, Buildkite, Bazel).

- Experience with test automation dashboards, logging, and reporting infrastructure (e.g., Grafana, Looker, Datadog, JIRA).

- Experience developing or testing automotive software across embedded and system levels.

- Strong cross-functional communication skills; able to work collaboratively across software, hardware, autonomy, DevOps, and product teams.

Point Digital Finance is expanding its Information Security function, and this is the team's first dedicated monitoring and response hire - a high-visibility role with immediate, measurable impact. We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD
Full-time employees qualify for our comprehensive benefits package, including:

• Health, dental and vision insurance

• Paid time off

• Annual CEU allowance

• 401K

• Supplies and other perks

• Malpractice coverage

title: Software Engineer, Payments Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands - including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank - to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

The agent must collect and use a card number but can never see it. This work sits across four hard technical domains: payments, security, real-time voice, and LLMs. Voice is the core challenge. A caller speaks or types a card number in a live, low-latency audio stream, and the digits must never reach the model, while the model stays on the call.

Sierra owns every system that touches card data, and one small team owns it end to end across three workstreams: Platform, Product, and Safety & Integrity. Customers keep their own telephony and payment gateways. Payments is live in production for some of the largest consumer enterprises, on a platform that handles hundreds of millions of calls a year. The platform is certified to PCI DSS Level 1.

- Build real-time card capture for voice: intercept keypad and spoken digits in a live audio stream, upstream of the agent runtime in a network-segmented environment, while the LLM stays live on the call. Make it work across every telephony provider and protocol Sierra supports.

- Build and extend the tokenization platform: agents receive and send short-lived tokens, and the platform swaps a token for the real value only when it calls the customer's payment gateway.

- Own the payments egress control plane: every destination for card data is approved, versioned with the agent release, and enforced by infrastructure below the application, not by convention.

- Make payment actions correct: an at-most-once action primitive in the Agent SDK, validated amounts and items, and monitoring that compares what the agent said about a payment with what really happened.

- Keep card data out of places it should not be: deterministic detection in the agent's hot path that catches what general-purpose models miss. No LLM, including any we build ourselves, ever sees a plaintext card number.

- Make payments self-serve: one payments API across Agent Studio, the Agent SDK, and Ghostwriter, Sierra's agent-building agent; gateway middleware that developers write against tokens; and support for single-tenant and customer-cloud deployments. Any team can add payments to an agent without a payments engineer in the loop.

- Grow the platform beyond cards: extend tokenization into a privacy vault for all PII.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

- 5+ years building backend, platform, or infrastructure systems, with a track record of shipping and operating high-reliability services in production.

- A deep security instinct. You design as though every component will eventually be compromised, and you reason naturally about blast radius, least privilege, and making bad states impossible rather than reacting to them.

- Rigor abo

title: Security Engineer Internship
description:
Security Engineer
Overview: Supply Chain Security and Compliance
The Security Engineer is a critical role responsible for implementing and enforcing robust security practices across our entire integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. You will safeguard e-commerce transactions, secure internal tool integrations, and establish the trust framework for our AI agent operations, ensuring compliance with global regulatory standards like PCI-DSS and GDPR.
Internship Details

• Duration: 3 months (extendable based on performance and project scope)

• Start Date: Immediate

• Location: Remote

• Stipend: Unpaid initially; may convert to a paid internship, full-time role, or even direct client absorption (FTE) based on your performance

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will secure all layers of the application, from the Next.js frontend to the NestJS modular monolith and the cloud infrastructure.

• Security Architecture & Threat Modeling: Perform vulnerability assessments, code reviews, and threat modeling for all new features and systems, focusing on the critical MES $\rightarrow$ WMS $\rightarrow$ OMS business process flow.

• Compliance Enforcement: Lead the implementation and auditing of security controls necessary for PCI-DSS compliance (for Payment module) and GDPR compliance (for user/tenant data handling).

• Access Control & Authentication: Implement and manage secure API authentication methods, including OAuth 2.0 and SAML, utilizing Authentik/Ory Kratos and leveraging PostgreSQL's Row-Level Security (RLS) for tenant isolation.

• Secrets & Encryption: Manage secrets and key rotation using Vault, define and enforce encryption protocols for data both in transit and at rest, and manage certificates via Traefik.

• Abuse Prevention: Implement and monitor controls for API rate limiting, Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules, and traffic monitoring to prevent abuse and denial-of-service attacks.

• Incident Response: Develop and practice incident investigation and response protocols. Conduct security awareness training for development and operations teams.

Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess hands-on security experience with our core stack and compliance tools:

• Platform Security: Node.js/NestJS security best practices, Next.js/React security, PostgreSQL RLS.

• Compliance Focus: Experience with PCI-DSS and GDPR controls and auditing.

• Authentication & Access: OAuth 2.0, SAML, JWT, Authentik/Ory Kratos.

• Secrets & Infrastructure: HashiCorp Vault, Docker, Terraform.

• Monitoring & Assessment: Tools for Static/Dynamic Application Security Testing (SAST/DAST).

AI Agent Security
You will be responsible for securing the emerging AI ecosystem.

• Agent Trust Framework: Establish security boundaries for the AI agent interfaces, ensuring agents (built with LangChain/AutoGen) operate within strict permissions when accessing supply chain data (WMS, OMS).

• Prompt Injection Prevention: Implement validation and sanitization techniques to mitigate prompt injection and data exfiltration risks in user-facing LLM interactions.

Success Metrics & Career Path
Performance will be measured by:

• Security Scorecard: Reduction in identified vulnerabilities from assessments and code reviews (SAST/DAST).

• Compliance Audits: Successful passing of regular PCI-DSS and GDPR audits.

• Incident Handling: Speed and effectiveness of security incident investigation and remediation.

Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Solution Architect or Head of Technology, working closely with the development and DevOps teams to embed security into the CI/CD pipeline.

title: Regulatory Compliance Manager
description:
About Onward

At Onward, we're nurturing wellbeing - one ride, one visit, one moment of connection at a time. Our door-through-door Companion rideshare services and transportation management platform help individuals with mobility and cognitive challenges access healthcare, community resources, and daily essentials. We work with healthcare systems, PACE programs, public transportation agencies, and health plans to improve care access, reduce missed appointments, and relieve the burden of caregiving.

If you thrive in fast-moving environments, love wearing multiple hats, want to help shape a category-defining business and lead a high-performing team, we want to talk.

Reports To : COO

Pay Range: $85,000 - $105,000 + equity

Location: 100% Remote, minimal travel

About the role

Execute the Compliance Work Behind a Growing Multi-State Technology-Enabled Transportation Network

Onward is building the infrastructure that helps people reliably access healthcare, partnering with healthcare providers and transit agencies to deliver transportation across a growing network of regulated markets.

As we expand into new geographies and programs, compliance is increasingly critical to how quickly we can launch, how reliably we operate, and how confidently we can scale.

We're hiring a Regulatory Compliance Manager to manage and execute Onward's day-to-day regulatory compliance work across new and existing markets. This is a hands-on individual contributor role working closely with Operations, Legal, Recruiting, Product, Sales, and other teams to ensure regulatory requirements are understood, translated into operational processes, completed, and documented.

This role is best suited for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable owning complex compliance work across multiple jurisdictions and programs. On any given week, that may mean researching requirements for an upcoming launch, submitting a regulatory filing, following up on an expiring driver credential, preparing audit documentation, or improving the systems and workflows we use to manage compliance at scale.

What you'll do

Market Launch & Regulatory Readiness

• Manage regulatory readiness for new-market launches from research through operational implementation, including applicable state, county, and local requirements.

• Identify company, driver, vehicle, training, screening, permitting, reporting, and other regulatory requirements and translate them into clear operational processes, owners, controls, and timelines .

• Coordinate applications, approvals, registrations, permits, and other launch requirements with Operations, Legal, Recruiting, Product, Finance, and other cross-functional teams.

• Maintain launch-readiness plans and drive multiple compliance workstreams, dependencies, and deadlines through completion.

• Identify potential compliance risks or launch blockers early and escalate unclear, high-risk, or legally sensitive matters to Operations, Legal, or leadership as appropriate.

• Ensure required compliance documentation, approvals, permits, registrations, and other launch dependencies are complete and organized before go-live.

Driver & Ongoing Compliance

• Manage ongoing driver and vehicle compliance across active markets, including insurance, vehicle registration, driver's license requirements, background checks, required training, screenings, and other market-specific requirements.

• Monitor expirations and recurring requirements and follow up directly with drivers and internal teams to ensure requirements are completed on time.

• Maintain accurate and audit-ready compliance records across markets.

• Improve the systems, controls, trackers, alerts, and workflows used to manage compliance, with a focus on creating scalable, repeatable processes and reducing unnecessary manual work.

• Partner with Recruiting, Operations, Product, and other teams to operationalize new or changing driver compliance requirements.

Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is seeking a Co-Op, Electron Microscopy to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. This co-op supports advanced SEM characterization workflows across powdered materials and thin films, working alongside synthesis, characterization, and ML scientists to turn physical experiments into high-quality data.

The work is hands-on and instrument-heavy: acquiring imaging and compositional data, refining methods, and iterating on protocols that feed Lila's materials discovery platform. It suits a PhD student who wants depth in microstructural analysis and sees how characterization data drives AI-guided materials research.

What You'll Be Building

• Design and execute SEM-based characterization workflows across diverse chemistries and form factors

• Operate electron microscopy instrumentation under the guidance of staff scientists

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Currently enrolled in a PhD in Materials Science, Physics, or a related field

title: Co-Op, SCADA Engineer

Your Impact at LILA

Lila's SCADA system spans cloud and on-premise infrastructure: Ignition gateways on EC2, a historian on RDS PostgreSQL, MQTT brokers, and edge nodes at each site. Today no single view shows the health of all of it, so the team learns about failures from users rather than from monitoring.

As a co-op on the Hardware & Controls Engineering team, you will build that view: a live connectivity diagram showing how every piece connects and which links are up, backed by dashboards covering database, gateway, and edge node health. The work is read-only end to end, with read-only AWS access and SELECT-only database access, so you can explore the full system safely.

You will be based at our Alewife site in Cambridge, working alongside controls engineers and the IT/OT team. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end.

What You'll Be Building

• Build a live topology view of edge nodes, brokers, gateways, and databases with per-link status and last-seen timestamps

• Surface RDS PostgreSQL health: CPU, memory, storage growth, connection counts, replication lag, and slow queries

• Dashboard Ignition gateway and EC2 metrics, including JVM heap, tag quality, Sparkplug birth and death rates, and scan timing

• Monitor on-premise edge nodes for reachability, uptime, resource use, and last publish time

• Integrate existing sources (CloudWatch, Performance Insights, Ignition gateway metrics, broker status) into one interface

• Document the setup so the team can extend and maintain it after the term ends

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field

• Available full time for the Spring 2027 co-op term, on-site at Alewife

• Proficiency in Python for scripting and data collection

• Comfortable working in Linux from the command line

• Working knowledge of networking fundamentals: IP addressing, subnets, ports, and routing

• Clear written communication for documenting dashboards and findings

Bonus Points For

• Exposure to AWS, particularly EC2, RDS, CloudWatch, or IAM

• Experience with Grafana, Prometheus, or similar observability tooling

• Familiarity with Ignition, MQTT or Sparkplug, or other industrial SCADA tooling
